title: edge proxy header fragmentation causing 502/504 waves and amplified retries during tenant failover
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Summary:
During a customer escalation where Hosted capacity briefly degraded and requests were routed to Dedicated fallback nodes, we observed a correlated spike of 502/504 responses and long client-side timeouts. The spike amplified because client SDKs retried aggressively, producing a retry storm that pushed more traffic to the fallback path and worsened the errors.

Observed behavior and hypothesis:
- Errors were concentrated on requests carrying very long Authorization and X-Tenant-Meta headers (some enterprise tenants send large JWTs + custom metadata).
- The edge proxy in the Hosted front door occasionally split or truncated large header frames when TLS session resumption and HTTP/2 frame coalescing interacted with our older connection buffer settings. Truncated headers reached the origin with malformed header sets, causing backends to return 502/504 or to abort during header parse.
- When the control plane detected host overload it shifted traffic to Dedicated pools that run a slightly different proxy configuration (older buffer defaults). That routing change exposed the header-fragmentation bug more often.
- Clients seeing 5xx/timeouts retried normally; retries were uncoordinated and lacked tenant-level hysteresis, producing amplification and KV-cache thrashing on the Dedicated nodes.

Why this is unique/urgent:
- This is not a pure runtime model failure or KV cache corruption; it's an edge protocol/byte-framing interaction that only surfaces under (1) large headers, (2) TLS session resumption with specific ciphers, and (3) fallback routing to pools with different proxy knobs. The combination makes it reproducible only in production-like traffic and is not caught by standard unit tests.

Scope of work (high level):
1) Hotfix: increase edge proxy header buffer and parsing resilience on Hosted front door and Dedicated fallback pools; add defensive reassembly logic to reject truncated header frames earlier with a 400 (fast-fail) rather than proxied 5xx.
2) Retry safety: add tenant-scoped retry-hysteresis at the admission controller to suppress aggressive retries for tenants that have >X transient 5xx within Y seconds.
3) Observability: emit header_length, header_truncation_count, transport-session-resume flag, per-tenant retry-rate, and per-pool malformed-header ratio to Datadog; add dashboard and alert with runbook link.
4) SDK guidance: short-term doc and sample code to recommend smaller custom metadata or use ephemeral tokens for large tenants; longer-term, standardize idempotency-key placement in request body (not headers) for large payloads.
5) Postmortem and tests: add integration tests simulating TLS session resume + large headers; run against Dedicated config matrix to catch asymmetric behavior.

Implementation notes and safety plan:
- We'll ship a two-step deploy: (A) patch proxy config to increase header buffer and enable defensive header validation (canary 3% edge traffic in eu-west1), and (B) deploy tenant-level retry-hysteresis to the admission controller behind a feature flag. Both changes have immediate revertability.
- Runtime changes are minimal; no model weights or serving runtime kernels touched. We aim for runtime-1.23 patch release for the proxy and admission-controller flip.
- Rollout timeline: canary -> 1 region -> global in 24–36 hours if telemetry shows improvements. If malformed-header ratios don't drop, rollback and revert to observability-only state and escalate to infra-networking for deeper TCP/TLS frame tracing.

Artifacts & links:
- Temporary investigation dashboard (Datadog): https://datadog.example/redwood/edge-header-fragmentation (placeholder)
- Draft PR for proxy buffer + defensive parse: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/## (placeholder)
- Admission-controller RT-hysteresis PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/## (placeholder)
- Customer escalation thread (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-thread (placeholder)

Acceptance criteria:
- Malformed-header ratio falls to <0.01% of pre-incident baseline in canary region within 6 hours of deploy.
- Per-tenant retry amplification (retry-rate/initial-failure-rate) decreases by at least 60% for affected tenants.
- No regression in normal request latency P95 (>1% change triggers rollback).
- Observability emits new metrics for at least 48 hours post-rollout and a short postmortem is published.

Rollforward/rollback guidance:
- If canary shows improvement and latency stable -> proceed to region and global rollouts.
- If retries drop but latency regresses beyond SLAs -> revert buffer increase and enable only header-validation fast-fail; iterate with networking team.
- If malformed headers persist -> enable forced tenant-quencher admission (aggressive short-circuit) for top 3 noisy tenants and continue investigation.

Notes for support/SRE on-call:
- When triaging: capture raw front-door connection logs with TLS session resume bit + header lengths for offending requests. Add filter by tenant ID and timestamp.
- Charms: use the temporary tracing agent to dump byte-level frames for a sample request to reproduce on staging.
